title: Sales Enablement Prospect Kit - Positioning, Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview:
This prospect kit is a single-stop reference for Sales, SDRs, Solutions Engineers, and Partner reps engaging enterprise and mid-market prospects. It bundles: positioning & messaging, competitor differentiation, a pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance and objection handling, two brief case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations. Use the sections below to prepare calls, tailor slide decks, or share short follow-ups with prospective technical and business stakeholders.

Audience and use cases:
- Audience: Head of Product, ML Engineering, Platform, CTO, Infrastructure/Cloud Architects, Procurement, Security.
- Typical use cases: evaluation of hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments; cost/latency trade-offs; compliance and on-prem requirements; procurement and SSO/KMS gating.

1) Positioning & Core Messaging
- One-liner: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes scalable, reliable, and cost-effective LLM serving predictable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

- Problem statement (concise): Teams building LLM features face unpredictable inference costs, brittle performance across models/hardware, and onerous ops overhead to maintain SLAs in production.

- Value pillars (use these verbatim in early outreach or slide headers):
  - Predictable Economics: usage & reserved capacity options, transparent token-level cost breakdowns, and Optimize tooling to cut unit costs.
  - Production Reliability: SLA-backed Dedicated options, model fallbacks, automatic routing and graceful degradation.
  - Developer Productivity: a single API surface, SDKs, examples, and rollout controls for fast iteration.
  - Security & Compliance: private deployments, customer-managed KMS/HSM, audit logs and SOC/ISO evidence packages.

- Elevator pitch (30s): "Redwood gives engineering teams a unified runtime and control plane to serve LLMs consistently - whether you want the fastest path to production with our hosted API, the predictability of reserved Dedicated capacity, or compliance-minded Private deployments. We reduce token costs with smart batching/caching and keep apps reliable with automatic fallbacks and detailed observability."

- Messaging by stakeholder:
  - CTO / Platform Lead: emphasize predictable throughput, multi-environment parity, rollout controls (canary/A-B), and billing visibility.
  - ML Engineer: emphasize model catalog, quantization recommendations, KV cache, continuous batching, and kernel-level optimizations.
  - Security / Compliance: focus on VPC/private control plane, KMS integration, audit logs, SOC/ISO artifacts and customer-managed key options.
  - Procurement / Finance: highlight pricing models (usage vs committed), cost visibility, and discounting structure for committed spend.

2) Competitive Briefs (short, battle-tested talking points)
- Versus general cloud AI endpoints (AWS/Azure/GCP managed endpoints):
  - Differentiator: Redwood provides a unified dev experience across hosted, dedicated, and private with production-first optimizations (continuous batching, KV cache).
  - Win themes: lower per-token cost at scale, predictable reserved capacity, and first-class model routing/fallback policies.
  - Loss risks: hyperscalers win on bare metal customizability and breadth of cloud services; counter by emphasizing our runtime micro-optimizations and faster time-to-productive-inference.

- Versus managed LLM API providers (single-API vendors):
  - Differentiator: choice and control - customers can start on hosted and then migrate to Dedicated/Private without API rewrite.
  - Win themes: migration parity, observability tied to unit economics, and enterprise SLAs.
  - Loss risks: single-vendor providers may have proprietary models with accuracy advantages; counter by highlighting model catalog and Redwood's support for curated/verified open models plus eval tooling.

- Versus self-hosted open-source runtimes (internal infra):
  - Differentiator: operational burden - Redwood handles kernel selection, autoscaling, fallbacks, and prebuilt observability; faster time to reliable production.
  - Win themes: reduced engineering ops, predictable TCO, and access to Optimize recommendations.
  - Loss risks: internal teams may prefer owning everything; counter by discussing hybrid deployment (Private) and migration paths that preserve customer controls.

3) Pitch Deck Outline (12-15 slides; recommended speaker notes per slide)
- Slide 1: Title + 1-line value prop + logo
- Slide 2: Customer pain (latency, cost, reliability) + 1-2 quotes/data points
- Slide 3: Redwood snapshot (what we do, deployment modes)
- Slide 4: How it works (runtime + compilation + smart routing + caching) - include simple diagram (textual placeholder)
- Slide 5: Performance & cost wins (tokens/sec, avg-cost/token reductions) - include benchmark summary (hosted vs Dedicated)
- Slide 6: Security & compliance (Private deployment, KMS/HSM, audit logs)
- Slide 7: Observability & ops (Console screenshots or mocked metrics)
- Slide 8: Pricing & consumption models (usage vs committed) + example TCO math for a reference workload
- Slide 9: Case studies (2 short customer stories)
- Slide 10: Deployment options & migration path (Proof-of-concept -> Pilot -> Production)
- Slide 11: SLA, support tiers, and rollout cadence
- Slide 12: Next steps / ask (trial, POC criteria, timeline)

Speaker notes guidance: always tailor slides 2 and 9 to prospect vertical and include explicit asks on slide 12 (e.g., ask for access to sample traffic, security questionnaire).

4) Pricing Guidance & Objection Handling
- Pricing models (short):
  - Hosted: pay-as-you-go per-token + per-embedding units. Best for quick evaluation and early production.
  - Dedicated: reserved capacity (monthly/annual) with predictable throughput and reduced per-token costs. Good for sustained production traffic.
  - Private: enterprise licensing + platform fee for on-prem/VPC installations. Includes optional support and retention add-ons.

- Representative pricing examples (present as illustrative math during calls):
  - Example A (Early-stage app, hosted): 200M inference tokens/month -> $X (show break-down: prompt tokens vs decode tokens)
  - Example B (Sustained production, dedicated): committed 2x A100-equivalent capacity -> monthly seat/commit discount reduces effective unit cost by ~30% (numbers calibrated per deal).

- Discounting and procurement: standard playbook is higher discount tiers for 12-24 month committed spend, professional services bundled for Private deployments, and enterprise SLA add-ons available. Procurement timelines: 4-8 weeks average for mid-market, 2-3 months for enterprise.

- Common pricing objections and scripts:
  - "We can self-host cheaper": ask for their end-to-end TCO (ops engineers, SLA costs, spike handling); show predictable Dedicated pricing and Optimize tooling that reduces token costs.
  - "We need absolute lowest latency": verify latency SLO needs; propose Dedicated in-region capacity or Private deployment with colocated hardware.
  - "Vendor lock-in concerns": emphasize identical API surface across deployment modes and migration path; offer short-term pilot contract.

5) Case Studies (two short vignettes for slide use and one-pager copy)
- Case Study 1: Conversational Customer Support SaaS (Mid-market)
  Owner: Solutions Engineering
  Summary: Reduced per-conversation inference cost by 42% and 99th percentile latency from 420ms to 200ms after migrating hot routes to Dedicated pools and enabling KV prefix caching.
  Key metrics: 42% unit cost reduction, 52% improvement in 99th pct latency, 6-week pilot -> production.
  Quote: "Redwood let us scale with predictable pricing and no surprise bills." - Head of Platform

- Case Study 2: Regulated Financial Data Provider (Enterprise)
  Owner: Enterprise Sales
  Summary: Needed on-prem deployment and HSM integration for model inference on sensitive customer data. Deployed Private (air-gapped) with customer-managed KMS and audit logging; passed internal security review and regulatory audit.
  Key metrics: Successful SOC2 evidence mapping, 3-month deployment timeline, full audit log retention per policy.
  Quote: "The Private deployment matched our security posture without delaying product timelines." - CTO

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (Technical + Procurement Concerns)
- Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
  A: Yes. Private and Dedicated deployments support integrations with customer KMS and HSMs; hosted customers can use envelope encryption with customer keys for data at rest.

- Q: Can we run Redwood in our VPC or on-prem?
  A: Yes. We offer a Private deployment model (VPC and optional on-prem package). We provide a private control plane and can execute air-gapped installs with professional services.

- Q: What audit and compliance artifacts are available?
  A: We provide SOC2/ISO artifacts for enterprise customers under NDA, audit logging streams, and per-request traceability in the Console.

- Q: How is customer data handled for hosted customers?
  A: By default, hosted inference data is isolated per tenant; we provide configurable data-retention policies and options for data deletion. Sensitive PII handling is controlled by customer-configured pipelines; for regulated workloads we recommend Private deployment.

- Q: How do you handle vulnerability disclosures and patching?
  A: We maintain an internal Secure SDLC, monthly vulnerability scanning, and a public CVE response process for critical issues. Private customers can request patch timelines in SLAs.

- Q: What network controls are available for Private/Dedicated?
  A: VPC peering, private link equivalents, IP allowlists, and mutually authenticated mTLS between control plane components; per-deployment network hardening checklists are available in engineering runbooks.

7) Enablement Checklist for Reps and SEs (pre-call / pre-demo)
1. Identify stakeholder map and top 3 success metrics (latency, cost, uptime).
2. Confirm deployment preference (hosted / dedicated / private).
3. Request sample traffic or representative payloads if possible (for realistic benchmarking).
4. Prepare cost-comparison TCO slide with conservative assumptions.
5. Share security FAQ and offer to route to security SME for deep conversations.
6. Propose clear POC acceptance criteria and timeline (suggested: 4-6 week pilot with success metrics).
